meta.description: Share your photos at full quality with the settings behind every shot. Join communities, enter photo contests, find photographers on the map and plan your Milky Way shoot.

landing.meta_description: Share your photos at full quality with the settings behind every shot. Join communities, enter photo contests, find photographers on the map and plan your Milky Way shoot.
landing.title: Where photographers meet.
landing.lead: Share your frames uncropped, at full quality. Show the camera and settings behind each shot; join communities, enter contests and message photographers where you're heading.
landing.exif_body: Shutter speed, aperture, ISO, camera and lens are read from the photo itself. Nobody has to ask how a shot was made.
landing.exif_point_quality: Blurry, tiny or blown-out photos don't get published.
landing.exif_point_uncropped: Nothing is ever cropped; every photo shows in its own aspect ratio.
landing.exif_point_location: Location data inside a photo is never shown without your approval.
landing.community_title: Start your community, run your contest.
landing.community_body: Set up your club or association, choose admins, share news and photos. Entrants don't need to join the community; sharing the link is enough.
landing.jury_body: Give each judge a weight; scores are collected on anonymous entries.
landing.public_body: Anyone verifies their email and votes; one person, one vote.
landing.contest_empty: No contests are open right now. Be the first to run one.
landing.map_title: Find the photographer where you're heading.
landing.map_body: See photographers and geotagged photos on a world map. Message public profiles about the road up, the best light, where to park. Local knowledge is one message away.
landing.map_privacy: Profile locations are rounded to about 5 km. A first message goes as a request; the conversation opens only if they accept.
landing.chat_1: I'll be in the Kaçkar Mountains in early October. Which plateau for the Milky Way?
landing.chat_2: Go up to Pokut. New moon, no light pollution; the core is southwest around 9 pm.
landing.sky_title: When and where is the Milky Way?
landing.sky_body: The sky planner works out the best shooting window, the Moon's phase and the core's direction for any night. The values beside this were just calculated in your browser.
landing.sky_ar: On mobile, point your phone at the sky: tonight's path of the core and the Moon appears over the camera view.
landing.guide_body: From the Milky Way to fast sports, portraits to fireworks: starting settings, common mistakes and calculators for every scenario.
landing.guide_npf_example: 24 MP full frame, 14 mm, f/1.8: stars stay as points
landing.pricing_title: Use it free, go Pro if you like.

faq.free_a: Yes. Sharing, communities, contests, messages and every tool are free. Pro only removes ads and adds a few small extras.
faq.rights_a: You do. Fotografya uses your photos only to show them on the site and in the app; it doesn't sell them or use them for anything else.
faq.location_a: GPS data inside a photo is removed on publishing and never shown without your approval. If you choose to appear on the map, your location is rounded to about 5 km.
faq.contests_a: Anyone with an account; you don't need to join the community. You enter each contest with a single photo. Voting in a public vote doesn't even need an account, just a verified email.
faq.formats_a: JPEG, PNG, WebP and HEIC, at least 1 MB with a long edge of 2000 px or more. Sharpness and exposure are checked automatically on upload.

landing.planner_season: The core doesn't rise in darkness tonight; above is the next good night.
landing.planner_never: At this latitude the core doesn't rise high enough in a dark sky in the coming months.

tools.title: Calculators
tools.npf_lead: The longest exposure that keeps stars as points. The NPF rule is far more reliable than the 500 rule on modern high-resolution sensors.
tools.npf_note: Pixel pitch {pitch} µm. The core sits 29° south of the celestial equator, so it allows a slightly longer exposure. The 500 rule trails stars at high resolution.
tools.dof_lead: How much stays sharp in front of and behind your focus point.
tools.dof_hyperfocal_tip: Focus at the hyperfocal distance ({h}) and everything from {half} to infinity is sharp.
tools.nd_lead: Converts the shutter speed you metered without the filter into the time needed with it.
tools.nd_bulb: For anything over 30 seconds, use Bulb mode and a remote release.

planner.title: Sky planner
planner.lead: How the Milky Way core, the Moon and the Sun move on the night and place you pick. Best window: the core at least 10° above the horizon, a fully dark sky and the Moon below the horizon.
planner.why_moon: The Moon is too bright and up while the core is visible. Try a date near the new moon.
planner.why_core: The core doesn't rise above the horizon from here on this date.
planner.why_dark: The sky doesn't get fully dark while the core is high enough.
planner.chart_hint: Tap and drag on the chart to pick a time. The shaded area is astronomical darkness.
planner.compass_label: Sky compass at the selected time
planner.accuracy: Times are in your device's time zone. Positions are accurate to ±0.6° for the Moon and ±0.2° for the Sun and core; in mountains the visible rise and set can shift by a few minutes.
